Article 3. Registration. Registration is open to new and old students who have satisfied the admission requirements. For on-site registration, students should enroll at the Office of the Registrar and register only in those subjects approved by the Registration Adviser/Program Coordinator/College Dean, as evidenced by their initials on the registration form. Sec. 1. Late Registration. The students are still allowed to register one (1) week after the last day of the regular registration period. Late registrants are charged a fine of P500.00. (BOR Resolution 1046 s 2012)

Sec. 2. Deferment of Enrolment. In the event that a qualified freshman applicant, who, for a valid reason, cannot enroll during the semester initially applied for, may petition for deferment of enrolment to the succeeding semester by writing to the University Registrar, provided that the applicant would not take any academic subjects in another college/ university during the deferment period.

Sec. 3. Refunding of Fees.

SECTION: Chapter 3 | Article 2. Admission Requirements
Article 2. Admission Requirements

Sec. 1. LSPU Entrance Examination Instrument, Policies and Guidelines for Admission, and Retention (CMO 105, s. 2015)

1.1. Accommodation Capacity. Admission to this University shall be limited to the number of students for whom adequate facilities and competent faculty members are available to provide better instruction.

1.2. Free Higher Education. All students who are either currently enrolled at the time of the affectivity of the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act of 2017 or Unified Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education Act, or UniFAST (Republic Act No.

10687) shall enroll at any time after that in a course leading to a bachelor’s degree in the University shall be exempt from paying tuition and other school fees for units enrolled in.

1.3. Institutional Qualifications. Students are eligible to receive the benefits stipulated in 1.2. provided that they qualify the admission and retention policies of the University.

Sec. 2. Admission and Testing

2.1. Non-discriminatory Admission. No student shall be denied admission to the University by reason of age, sex, gender, nationality, belief, or political affiliation.

SECTION: Chapter 4 | Article 3. GSAR Admission Requirements, Policies, and Registration
Any bachelor’s degree holder from various colleges or universities shall apply for admission and comply with all the course requirements where the student intends to enroll.

2.2. An undergraduate without specialization may be admitted but is required to earn 18 education units and preferably a holder of a license in teaching before admitted to the Master of Arts in Education program. The student must also be a PRC license holder.

2.3. Master of Arts in Education (M.A.Ed.). Enrollee in any field of concentration shall have 12 units of undergraduate academic background related to the intended major course or at least two (2) years of experience teaching the subject or practicing the field.

2.4 Master of Science in Agriculture (M.S.A.) / Master of Science in Fishery. A non-agriculture graduate has to earn 18 units in an agriculture course before admittance to MSA. Alternatively, an enrollee in any field of concentration shall have 12 units of undergraduate academic background related to the intended major course.

2.5. The list of officially enrolled students shall be furnished by the registrar through the Dean/Assistant Dean.

To enroll at LSPU-LB campus, follow these steps:

1. Apply online for completion of INC or 4.0 grade by submitting the complete requirements to the subject teacher, then log in to the portal in the LSPU online system (Step 1: Apply online for completion, processing time: 5 minutes).

2. Submit the required documents for enrollment, such as enrolment slip, certificates, and other documents as specified, either on the scheduled appointment date at the Office of the Registrar (for new and transferee students) or via the Student Web Portal (for old students).

3. Submit the hard copy of enrollment requirements or enlist subjects through the Student Web Portal (Step 1: Submission of enrolment requirements / subject enlistment, processing time: 8 minutes for new/transferee students, 3 minutes for old students).

4. Pay the assessed fees at the Accounting Office or Cashier.

5. View the Certificate of Registration (COR) on the portal or claim the printed copy at the Registrar.

6. For on-site registration, enroll only in subjects approved by the Registration Adviser/Program Coordinator/College Dean, as evidenced by their initials on the registration form.

7. Late registration is allowed up to one week after the last day of the regular registration period with a P500.00 fine.

8. If unable to enroll during the semester, petition for deferment of enrollment to the succeeding semester by writing to the University Registrar.

9. For international students, follow the specific procedures including submission of intention to enroll, application for conversion of visa, and compliance with medical requirements, facilitated by the IA Student Mobility.

Note: Ensure you meet the admission requirements and have all necessary documents ready for submission.

1. Apply online for completion of INC or 4.0 grade by submitting the complete requirements to the subject teacher, then log in to the portal in the LSPU online system (Step 1: Apply online for completion, processing time: 5 minutes).

2. Submit the required documents for enrollment, such as enrolment slip, certificates, and other documents as specified, either on the scheduled appointment date at the Office of the Registrar (for new and transferee students) or via the Student Web Portal (for old students).

3. Submit the hard copy of enrollment requirements or enlist subjects through the Student Web Portal (Step 1: Submission of enrolment requirements / subject enlistment, processing time: 8 minutes for new/transferee students, 3 minutes for old students).

4. Pay the assessed fees at the Accounting Office or Cashier.

5. View the Certificate of Registration (COR) on the portal or claim the printed copy at the Registrar.

6. For on-site registration, enroll only in subjects approved by the Registration Adviser/Program Coordinator/College Dean, as evidenced by their initials on the registration form.

7. Late registration is allowed up to one week after the last day of the regular registration period with a P500.00 fine.

8. If unable to enroll during the semester, petition for deferment of enrollment to the succeeding semester by writing to the University Registrar.

9. For international students, follow the specific procedures including submission of intention to enroll, application for conversion of visa, and compliance with medical requirements, facilitated by the IA Student Mobility.

Note: Ensure you meet the admission requirements and have all necessary documents ready for submission.
